--- page 1 ---
THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | AZ PE #48213 | CFDME-2025-041 rev A

To: Project file, CFDME-2025-041 (Ocotillo WUI, Phase 1) From: Gordon Selby, PE — The CFD Mechanical
Engineer, LLC Subject: Structural Wind-Load Basis Memo (SOW §3.2) Prepared: 10/09/2025. Basis of the
structural wind-load extraction called out in SOW §3.2 — ASCE 7-22 procedure, site parameters, velocity pressure,
and wall design pressures for the Ocotillo Additive Structures wall assembly at the Avra Valley WUI site.


1. Purpose and scope
This memo restates, in the firm's own words, the ASCE 7-22 procedure applied to the structural wind-load extraction
required under Section 3.2 of the signed Statement of Work (executed 2025-10-08). The output of that
extraction is the set of design wind pressures on the Ocotillo double-wythe printed-concrete wall assembly at the Avra
Valley WUI site, expressed both in US customary units (psf) and in SI (Pa) per the firm's Units and Conversions SOP.
The scope of this memo is limited to the structural load case defined in Section 3.2 of the SOW. It is not the wildfire
exposure matrix defined in Section 3.1 of the same SOW; the two load cases are physically and procedurally distinct,
and — as recorded in §5 below — a pressure or velocity reported from one may not be used to check the boundary
conditions of the other. External standards referred to in this memo (ASCE 7-22 §26 and §27) are summarized under
the firm's single-user license per the External Standards Digest (rev 1); no proprietary text is reproduced.

2. Site parameters
The site is the Ocotillo Additive Structures Sonoran-Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson (Avra Valley), Pima County,
Arizona. Site parameters used to enter the ASCE 7-22 wind procedure are as follows.

Parameter                                Value                                    Source
Site                                     Tucson, Arizona (Avra Valley WUI)        Project record
Risk Category                            II (ordinary occupancy)                  ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1
Basic wind speed, V                      96 mph (3-s gust)                        ASCE 7-22 Fig. 26.5-1B, Risk Cat II,
                                                                                  Tucson
Exposure Category                        Exposure C (open terrain with            ASCE 7-22 §26.7.3
                                         scattered obstructions)
Mean roof height, h                      6.4 m (≈ 21 ft)                          Ocotillo geometry
                                                                                  OAS-WUI-01_revC

The occupancy is ordinary and the structure does not fall within the definitions of Risk Category III or IV, so Risk
Category II governs. The Avra Valley parcel is open desert with scattered creosote, mesquite, and buffelgrass ground
cover extending well beyond 20·h upwind in all directions relevant to the design wind rose; there is no built or forested
surface roughness of the kind that would qualify the site as Exposure B, and the site is not on open water, so
Exposure C is the correct assignment per ASCE 7-22 §26.7.3.

2.1 Velocity-pressure exposure and topographic factors
Coefficient                              Value                                    Basis
K_z (velocity pressure exposure          K_z = 0.91                               ASCE 7-22 Table 26.10-1, Exposure
coefficient) at h = 6.4 m                                                         C, interpolated to h ≈ 21 ft
K_zt (topographic factor)                1.0                                      Essentially flat terrain; site does not
                                                                                  sit on a hill, ridge, or escarpment
                                                                                  meeting the §26.8.2 geometry test

Table 26.10-1 tabulates K_z for Exposure C at 15 ft (0.85) and at 20 ft (0.90). Linear interpolation to 21 ft gives 0.91,
which the firm adopts.

2.1a Ground elevation and directionality factors


--- page 2 ---
Coefficient                             Value                                    Basis
K_e (ground elevation factor)           K_e = 1.0                                Per ASCE 7-22 §26.9, K_e = 1.0 is
                                                                                 permitted at all elevations as a
                                                                                 conservative choice; the tabulated
                                                                                 value at the site's ~750 m ground
                                                                                 elevation would be approximately
                                                                                 0.92, so adopting K_e = 1.0 is
                                                                                 conservative here
K_d (wind directionality factor)        K_d = 0.85                               ASCE 7-22 Table 26.6-1, main
                                                                                 wind-force resisting systems —
                                                                                 buildings


3. Velocity pressure
The velocity pressure at mean roof height h = 6.4 m is computed per ASCE 7-22 Eq. 26.10-1:
q_z = 0.00256 · K_z · K_zt · K_e · V² = 0.00256 · 0.91 · 1.0 · 1.0 · (96)² = 21.5 psf. Per ASCE 7-22 the wind
directionality factor K_d is applied in the design pressure equation (not the velocity pressure equation).
Arithmetic check: 0.00256 × 0.91 = 0.0023296; × 96² = × 9216 = 21.469 psf, rounded to q_z = 21.5 psf. In SI, 21.5
psf × 47.88 Pa/psf ≈ 1029 Pa.

4. Windward wall design pressure
For the main wind-force resisting system on an enclosed rigid building, the wall pressure on the windward face is
taken as
p_w = q_z · G · C_p · K_d = 21.5 · 0.85 · 0.8 · 0.85 = 12.41 psf, reported as 12.4 psf, which is 594 Pa at 1 psf =
47.88 Pa.
Where:
• G = 0.85 — gust-effect factor for a rigid building (natural frequency > 1 Hz), ASCE 7-22 §26.11.1;
• C_p = 0.8 — external pressure coefficient for the windward wall of an enclosed building, ASCE 7-22 Figure
   27.3-1;
• K_d = 0.85 — as tabulated in §2.1a above.
Arithmetic check: 21.5 × 0.85 = 18.275; × 0.8 = 14.62; × 0.85 = 12.427 psf → rounded to 12.4 psf. Conversion: 12.4 ×
47.88 = 593.7 Pa → rounded to 594 Pa.

Pressure summary — Ocotillo wall assembly, mean roof height h = 6.4 m
Surface                 C_p                     Design pressure p =     US (psf)                SI (Pa)
                                                q_z · G · C_p · K_d
Windward wall           +0.8                    21.5 · 0.85 · 0.8 ·     +12.4 psf               +594 Pa
                                                0.85
Leeward wall            −0.5                    q_z · G · C_p · K_d = −7.8 psf                  −372 Pa
                                                1029 · 0.85 · (−0.50) ·
                                                0.85
Side walls              −0.7                    −0.7 · q_z · G · K_d    −10.86 psf              −520 Pa
Roof                    varies                  Per ASCE 7-22 Fig.      varies                  varies
                                                27.3-1 by roof slope
                                                and wind direction

Signs follow the ASCE convention: positive pressure acts toward the surface, negative pressure (suction) acts away
from the surface. The controlling load combinations for the wall panel and its ties are the strength-design
combinations of ASCE 7-22 Chapter 2 with the wind load W taken from this basis; those combinations are outside the
scope of this memo and will be applied in the structural check itself.


--- page 3 ---
Authority. The design pressures in the table above are the governing values for the Section 3.2 structural wind-load
extraction. Any surface pressure produced by the CFD probe extraction for this load case that does not agree in
magnitude with the corresponding row above shall be reconciled against this memo before appearing in any
client-facing deliverable. Peer-review item 9 tracks that reconciliation to close.

5. Section 3.1 versus Section 3.2 — the two load cases must not be conflated
This load case (SOW §3.2) is separate from the Section 3.1 wildfire exposure matrix. Section 3.1 runs at 5–12 m/s
(11.2–26.8 mph), where the velocity pressure is approximately
q_z ~ 0.00256 · 0.91 · (11.2 to 26.8)² ~ 0.29 to 1.68 psf ~ 14-80 Pa,
and windward wall loading is on the order of 60 Pa. A pressure reported from the §3.1 case cannot be checked
against the boundary conditions of the §3.2 case, and vice versa. The two must not be conflated.
Practically, this has two consequences for anyone reading downstream case files, probe rollups, or draft-report
tables:
1. A pressure reported at the wall surface of a Section 3.1 wildfire-matrix case that is on the order of tens of pascals is
consistent with the boundary conditions of that case and is not to be compared to the 594 Pa windward pressure of
this Section 3.2 case. 2. Section 3.2 results must be cross-checked against the boundary conditions documented in
this memo per the procedure in the firm's Units and Conversions SOP (§4) before rollup to any deliverable.
Both cases share the same wall assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC) and the same nominal site air density (1.2
kg/m³), but the physical regimes, boundary conditions, and reported quantities are otherwise disjoint.

6. References
External-standard references have been abstracted and cited per the firm's External Standards Digest (rev 1).
No proprietary text is reproduced. Digest citations used in this memo:
• ASCE 7-22, Chapter 26 — Wind Loads: General Requirements. §26.5 (basic wind speed maps for Risk
   Category I–IV), §26.6 (wind directionality factor K_d, Table 26.6-1), §26.7 (surface roughness and exposure
   category), §26.8 (topographic factor K_zt), §26.9 (ground elevation factor K_e; K_e = 1.0 permitted at all
   elevations as conservative), §26.10 (velocity pressure equation and Table 26.10-1 for K_z), §26.11 (gust-effect
   factor G for rigid buildings).
• ASCE 7-22, Chapter 27 — Wind Loads on Buildings: Main Wind Force Resisting System (Directional
   Procedure). §27.3 and Figure 27.3-1 (external pressure coefficients C_p for enclosed buildings — windward,
   leeward, side walls, and roof by slope and wind direction).
• CFDME External Standards Digest rev 1. Firm-internal restatements of the ASCE 7-22 §26 and §27
   provisions above; used as the working reference for this project.
• CFDME Units and Conversions SOP rev 2, §3 (1 psf = 47.88 Pa) and §4 (magnitude cross-check
   against boundary conditions before rollup).
• CFDME-2025-041 SOW, §3.2 - scope of the structural wind-load extraction; §3.1 - scope of the wildfire
   exposure matrix (referenced here only to record the boundary between the two cases).

        THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | Quota Remediation Procedure | rev 2 | Effective 07/01/2025 | Supersedes rev 1


Quota Remediation Procedure | rev 2 | Effective 07/01/2025
Joint authors: Marguerite Falk, PE (Technical Director and Reviewing Engineer) and Gordon Selby, PE (Owner and
Principal Engineer)
Applies to: all internal engineering staff of The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (trade name: The CFD ME)


1. Purpose
This procedure defines the strict ladder to be followed when the firm's Compensation and Quota Policy rev 3
triggers remediation for an internal engineer. It supersedes rev 1 in its entirety.
The firm's position on quota-shortfall response is stated in the compensation policy and repeated here so that any
operations lead, reviewing engineer, or owner who administers a ladder can read this document standalone: a
shortfall in billed revenue is first a question about assignment, staffing, and the composition of the firm's book of
business, and only after the full ladder has been worked does it become a question about the engineer's fit at the firm.
The ladder set out in Section 3 is the sole response protocol. It is a strict ordered sequence — the rungs are
numbered, and the numbering is normative, not descriptive.
The purpose of this document is to remove discretion at the point of decision. When the compensation policy's
monthly assessment routes a matter to remediation, the response is set: the operations lead opens the ladder at rung
1, works it through a full assessment cycle, and escalates to the next rung only if that cycle does not resolve the
shortfall. There is no branch, no substitution, and no first-response termination.

2. Trigger
The remediation ladder opens when the monthly quota-close assessment under Compensation Policy rev 3 §5
records two consecutive months below the billing quota for the same internal engineer. The billing quota is
$20,000/month per engineer, defined in Compensation Policy rev 3 §2.
The trigger is mechanical. It is read from the billed-revenue-by-engineer sheet maintained in /Firm/HR/Billing/
on the last business day of each calendar month. When the second consecutive below-quota month closes, the
operations lead routes the matter to this procedure and the ladder opens at rung 1. No other input — verbal report,
subjective assessment, client feedback, or peer complaint — opens the ladder.
The trigger is quota-specific. This procedure addresses billed-revenue shortfalls only. Concerns about engineering
quality, professional conduct, or fitness for duty are handled through separate channels and are not within the scope
of the ladder set out below.

3. Ladder
The ladder has three rungs. Rungs are numbered in strict order and may not be skipped. Each rung must run for
its full assessment cycle before the next rung is considered.

Rung 1 — Reassignment to Physical-Test Contract Management
The engineer is reassigned to manage physical-test contracts (e.g., ASTM E119 test coordination, wind-tunnel
campaign management, third-party lab liaison). During this rung the engineer is measured on the validation
schedule (on-time completion of test milestones, cleanliness of instrumentation and data hand-off, and report
turnaround) rather than the $20,000/month billing quota.
Assessment cycle: one full month.
Rung 1 is opened by a staffing decision memo that identifies the engineer, cites the below-quota months of record,
names the specific physical-test contract slot the engineer is being reassigned into (drawn from the Staffing and
Assignment Sheet), and states        the start date of the assessment cycle. The engineer's base compensation is
unchanged during this rung. The billing quota does not apply while the engineer is in rung 1; billing performance
during this cycle is not assessed.
At the close of the one-month assessment cycle, the operations lead records the validation-schedule outcome — met
or below — in the engineer's HR file. If the engineer meets the validation schedule for the cycle, the ladder closes and
the engineer either continues in the physical-test contract slot or returns to standard engagement assignment, at the


--- page 2 ---
owner's discretion. If the validation schedule is not met, the ladder advances to rung 2. Advancement requires a new
staffing decision memo citing rung 2.

Rung 2 — Technical Sales Rotation
If rung 1 does not resolve after a full assessment cycle, the engineer is moved into a technical sales role with an
annual booked-revenue target of 3× base salary. Base compensation remains unchanged during this rung.
Assessment cycle: one calendar year.
Rung 2 is opened by a staffing decision memo that identifies the engineer, cites the rung 1 outcome, names the
technical sales slot (drawn from the Staffing and Assignment Sheet), states       the annual booked-revenue target
expressed as 3× the engineer's current base salary, and states the start date of the twelve-month assessment cycle.
During rung 2 the engineer is measured on booked revenue against the annual target; the $20,000/month billing
quota does not apply, and validation-schedule metrics do not apply.
At the close of the twelve-month cycle, the operations lead records the booked-revenue outcome in the engineer's
HR file. If the annual target is met, the ladder closes and the engineer continues in the technical sales role or returns
to standard engagement assignment, at the owner's discretion. If the annual target is not met, the ladder advances to
rung 3. Advancement requires a new staffing decision memo citing rung 3.

Rung 3 — Offboard
If rung 2 does not resolve after a full year, the engineer is offboarded with standard severance and reference
support.
Rung 3 is opened by a staffing decision memo that identifies the engineer, cites the rung 2 outcome, states the
offboard date, and confirms severance and reference-support terms per the firm's standard offboarding schedule.
The memo is countersigned by the owner.

4. Rules of the Ladder
Rungs shall not be skipped. Each rung must run for a full cycle before the next is considered. Termination is not
available as a first response to a quota shortfall. Generic Performance Improvement Plans are not used.
The rules of the ladder are absolute:
• Order. The rungs run in the order 1 → 2 → 3. Rung 2 may not be opened without a completed rung 1 cycle
   recorded in the HR file. Rung 3 may not be opened without a completed rung 2 cycle recorded in the HR file.
• Full cycle. Rung 1 is one full month. Rung 2 is one full calendar year (twelve consecutive months from the start
   date named in the rung 2 memo). A rung is not "worked" until its full cycle has elapsed. Early advancement is
   prohibited.
• No skipping. No rung may be omitted. There is no discretionary shortcut from rung 1 to rung 3, and no shortcut
   from the trigger directly to rung 2 or rung 3.
• No first-response termination. Offboarding is available only at rung 3, and only after rungs 1 and 2 have each
   run to completion without resolution.
• No generic PIP. The firm does not use generic Performance Improvement Plans for quota shortfalls. The ladder
   set out in Section 3 is the sole response. A PIP is not substituted for a rung, appended to a rung, or issued in
   parallel with the ladder.
• Base compensation. Base salary is unchanged during rungs 1 and 2. The ladder does not adjust base
   compensation; it adjusts assignment and the metric against which the engineer is measured.
These rules are set to remove the two failure modes the firm has determined it will not accept: skipping to termination
without giving the engineer's assignment and staffing a fair chance to correct, and papering over an assignment or
staffing problem with a generic improvement plan that shifts the burden onto the engineer.

5. Records and Documentation
Each rung is opened by a staffing decision memo authored by the operations lead and countersigned by the owner
(Gordon Selby, PE) and, at rungs 1 and 2, by the Technical Director (Marguerite Falk, PE) in her administering
capacity. The memo cites:


--- page 3 ---
• The rung invoked (1, 2, or 3), by number.
• The assessment cycle applicable to that rung (one month for rung 1; one calendar year for rung 2; not applicable
   at rung 3 — the memo states the offboard date instead).
• The confirmed staffing slot for the engineer at rungs 1 and 2, drawn from and cross-referenced to the Staffing and
   Assignment Sheet           (/Firm/Ops/CFDME_staffing_assignments.xlsx). The memo states the
   specific validation-schedule slot for rung 1 or the specific technical sales slot for rung 2.
• The below-quota months of record that triggered the ladder (for the rung 1 memo), or the prior-rung outcome (for
   the rung 2 and rung 3 memos).
• The start date of the assessment cycle.
Staffing decision memos are retained in the engineer's HR file at /Firm/HR/ for the retention period stated in the
compensation policy. At the close of each rung's assessment cycle, the operations lead records the outcome — met
or below — in the same file, alongside the memo that opened the rung. When a ladder closes at any rung, the closure
is recorded in the HR file.
Access to remediation ladder records is limited to the owner, the operations lead, the engineer for that engineer's own
records, and the Technical Director in her capacity administering a ladder.

6. Related
• Compensation and Quota Policy rev 3 — /Firm/HR/CFDME_Compensation_Quota_Policy_rev3.pdf
   Defines       the $20,000/month billing quota, the monthly quota-close assessment, and the
   two-consecutive-months-below trigger that opens this procedure. States the firm's position that generic
   Performance Improvement Plans are not used and that termination is never the first response to a quota shortfall.
• Staffing and Assignment Sheet — /Firm/Ops/CFDME_staffing_assignments.xlsx. Master
   engineering roster showing current assignments, open positions, and validation-schedule slots. Source for the
   specific rung 1 physical-test contract slot and the specific rung 2 technical sales slot named in each staffing
   decision memo.

THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | Compensation and Quota Policy | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025 | Applies to: all internal engineering
                                                         staff



1. Purpose and Scope
This policy states the compensation structure, monthly billing quota, and quota-performance assessment procedure
that apply to every internal engineering position at The CFD ME, LLC. It supersedes rev 2 in its entirety.
The scope covers every W-2 engineering role — owner and principal engineer, technical director and reviewing
engineer, senior CFD engineer, and CFD engineer — whether resident in the Tucson office or working remotely. It
does not apply to contracted outside labor engaged under separate work orders, nor to non-engineering
administrative staff.
The policy is one of three internal-HR documents that jointly govern engineering-side quota, remediation, and
staffing. It is designed to be read alongside the Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2 and the Staffing and Assignment
Sheet.

2. Billing Quota
Each internal engineer carries a monthly billing quota of $20,000/month. Billable work is defined as engineer-hours
logged against a signed and current client engagement, at the billing rate for that engagement.
The quota is a floor, not a target ceiling. It is set at a level the firm has confirmed to be achievable given normal
workload allocation and the firm's active book of business, and is unchanged from the level in effect since the firm
staffed up beyond a single-owner configuration.

3. Definitions of Billable Work
Billable work is engineer-hours logged against an external client engagement where all of the following conditions are
met:
• The engagement is under a signed statement of work, master services agreement, or task order in force at the
   time the hour is logged.
• The engagement is current — not closed, not suspended for non-payment, and not out of scope of any active task
   order.
• The hour is charged at the billing rate designated for that engagement in the governing contract.
The following categories of work are explicitly not billable and do not count toward the quota:
• Internal training, including internal seminars, reading time on external standards, and mentoring or onboarding of
   other firm engineers.
• Firm standards work, including drafting, revising, and reviewing internal modeling standards, QA procedures, and
   standard operating procedures.
• Administrative work, including timesheet entry, expense reporting, procurement, and internal record-keeping.
• Marketing and business development, including proposal preparation, prospect calls, conference attendance, and
   outreach.
The above categories may be excluded from the non-billable list on a case-by-case basis when a specific internal
charge code has been designated for a defined initiative and communicated in writing by the owner. Absent such
designation, they are non-billable.

4. Compensation Structure
Compensation for internal engineering staff has two components:
• Base salary. Set by role and by written offer letter or subsequent written adjustment. Paid semi-monthly. The
   base salary is not tied to individual billed revenue.
• Firm-wide profit share. Distributed on a firm-wide basis according to the profit-share schedule maintained by the
   owner. All internal engineers who are employed at the close of the applicable distribution period participate. The
   profit-share pool is a function of firm profitability, not of any individual engineer's billed revenue.


--- page 2 ---
There are no individual commissions for internal engineers other than the reviewer commission for Marguerite Falk,
PE, described in her role letter and cross-referenced in Section 7. No individual engineer receives a percentage of the
revenue they personally bill.
The firm has deliberately declined to compensate engineers on personal-billing commission. Commission structures
introduce incentive tension between billable-work volume and engineering-work quality, which the firm has
determined it will not accept on the technical side of the practice.

5. Quota Performance Assessment
Quota performance is assessed monthly at close (last business day of each calendar month) by the operations lead
against the billing records in Firm/HR/Billing/. Two consecutive months below quota trigger the Quota Remediation
Procedure (rev 2 or current).
The operations lead's assessment reads the billed-revenue-by-engineer sheet as of the close of the calendar month,
compares each engineer's billed revenue for that month against the $20,000/month quota, and marks each engineer
as met or below for that month. The assessment is a mechanical read of the billing record. It is not a subjective
judgment about the engineer's work.
When an engineer is marked below for two consecutive months, the assessment routes the matter to the Quota
Remediation Procedure for opening of the remediation ladder. No other assessment output — verbal, written, or
otherwise — is used to initiate a response to a quota shortfall.

6. Remediation Procedure
The Quota Remediation Procedure establishes the sole firm response to consecutive quota shortfalls; consult that
document for the applicable ladder. Rung ordering is strict and rungs may not be skipped.

7. Reviewer Compensation Note
Marguerite Falk, PE serves as the firm's Technical Director and Reviewing Engineer and is compensated in part on
commission as a declared incentive under the terms of her role letter. The declared incentive tension between the
commissioned component of her compensation and her role as mandatory review gate on stamped deliverables is
managed through the stamp boundary: Gordon Selby, PE stamps CFD thermal analysis only; fire-resistance ratings
are certified separately by others (Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering). The stamp boundary is stated on every
CFD thermal deliverable that leaves the firm.
The reviewer-commission arrangement is limited to Marguerite Falk's role and is not extended to other internal
engineers. No other internal engineer receives a commissioned component of compensation.
The billing quota, monthly assessment, and remediation triggers are governed per Section 5 above.

8. Records
The following records are maintained in support of this policy:
• Engineer billing records by month. File: /Firm/HR/Billing/billing_by_engineer_2025.xlsx (current
   calendar year) and prior-year archives in the same directory. Maintained by the operations lead. Records billed
   revenue by engineer by month.
• Monthly quota-close assessments. Recorded by the operations lead on the last business day of each calendar
   month; retained in the HR file for the engineer.
• Remediation ladder records. When a remediation ladder is opened, the record of each rung's action, cycle
   duration, and outcome is maintained per the Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2.
• Role letters and compensation adjustments. Retained in each engineer's HR file.
Records are retained for the duration required by applicable law and by firm policy, whichever is longer. Access is
limited to the owner, the operations lead, the individual engineer for that engineer's own records, and Marguerite Falk
in her capacity as Technical Director for records relevant to a remediation ladder she is administering.

9. Related Documents
• Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2. File: /Firm/HR/CFDME_Remediation_Procedure_rev2.pdf. States
   the firm response to consecutive quota shortfalls.


--- page 3 ---
• Staffing and Assignment Sheet. File: /Firm/Ops/CFDME_staffing_assignments.xlsx. Master
   engineering roster showing current assignments, open positions, and validation-schedule slots. Used as the
   source for rung 1 reassignment slots.
Any staffing action arising from a quota shortfall is governed by the Quota Remediation Procedure cited above.

Signed:
_/s/ Gordon Selby, PE_
Gordon Selby, PE Owner and Principal Engineer The CFD ME, LLC AZ PE #48213
Effective: 07/01/2025

22:22 'Normal' The reported E is +13 min at the whole-minute values; the unrounded E is +12.94 min, which is about 11.0% of D against the 10% limit. The sign is positive: the model over-predicts endurance, which is non-conservative for a fire-resistance claim. Either value exceeds the 11.8-min criterion. The largest prediction that would have cleared the primary criterion is 129.8 min; if predictions are stated only in whole minutes, the largest whole-minute prediction that clears is 129 min, because 130 min gives |E| = 12 min > 11.8 min. That 129.8-min value would still be a resolved model error because |E| = 11.8 min > u_val = 9 min. To satisfy both the primary criterion and the secondary u_val test, S must lie between 109 min and 127 min; the current run at 131 min is 4 min above that upper bound.
28:28 'Normal' Both criteria are displaced by the same +13 min. A tie-only error or a single-point thermocouple-placement error would move the single-point criterion relative to the average and change the 45-min separation. It does not. The model is therefore transferring heat through the wall too slowly overall — or is being driven by too little effective furnace-side heat — in a common-mode way. The likely causes are the global thermal boundary condition, the temperature-dependent solid properties, contact resistance, or the conjugate-heat-transfer mesh, not the tie geometry or the choice of governing point.

## Findings (most serious first)

### 1. BLOCKING — The run is not the certified/tested assembly in plan size; the memo's "yes" on assembly identity is not supported and its own Table 1 contradicts it.

**Requirement.** Ironwood IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.1 states that the certification is based on a test “on a 3.05 m × 3.05 m non-load-bearing specimen of the assembly”; §1.2 states “Any deviation from the tabulated geometry places the assembly outside the scope of this certification.” Red Butte RBFMT-25-0918 §2 describes “One 3.05 m × 3.05 m (10 ft × 10 ft) specimen.” The task asks to “Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on.”

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §1: “The assembly in the run is the assembly the certification covers, within the certification’s tabulated scope.” §3 and Table 1 acknowledge that the Red Butte specimen was 3.05 m × 3.05 m while revC is a “1830 mm × 2745 mm × 305 mm panel.” §3 then says: “The certification table does not make plan size a scope parameter … If the certification is later read as requiring the 3.05 m plan size, that is a question for Ironwood, not a basis for this validation.”

**What it should be.** The run geometry is 1.83 m × 2.745 m × 0.305 m (plan area 5.02 m²), only 54 % of the 3.05 m × 3.05 m (9.30 m²) tested specimen. That is a material geometry deviation, not a through-wall detail. The memo should either (a) obtain written confirmation from Ironwood that plan size is not a certification scope parameter, or (b) state plainly that the run is outside the as-tested/certified specimen geometry, so the S/D comparison cannot be presented as a validation of the certified assembly. The top-line answer “yes” must not be given while the plan-size question is left to Ironwood; the task asked the memo to settle it.

**Evidence.** `Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Geometry/OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd`, `Document.xml`: `Width_mm = 1830`, `Height_mm = 2745`, `Thickness_mm = 305`, Description “Outer dims per WUI test panel: 1830 x 305 x 2745 mm.” Ironwood p.1 §1.1–§1.2; Red Butte p.1 §2. Plan area: 1.83 × 2.745 = 5.02 m² versus 3.05 × 3.05 = 9.30 m² (54 %).

### 2. BLOCKING — There is no documented E119 case setup, mesh, run log, or property/boundary-condition record; the memo's S is therefore not the documented S required by Validation Procedure §3, and the memo's “documented model-error finding” overstates the basis.

**Requirement.** Validation Procedure rev 2 §3: “S is the simulation prediction — the value produced by the CFD run using the model, mesh, solver, boundary conditions, and material properties documented in the report.” Every deliverable must present S, D, E, u_val “with a citation to the physical test report from which D is taken and to the run identifier from which S is taken.” Peer-review checklist item 7 requires confirmation of which OAS-WUI-01 revision matches the mesh-build timestamp in the case log. The technical-verification-review method requires “Not verified — item remains open” where the basis is missing; a missing case record cannot be closed as a documented finding.

**What the deliverable has.** §3 relies on “All case logs, the three-grid study and the deliverable manifest” to establish revC, but these are the wildfire LES artifacts. §5.3 itself states: “The only E119 companion artifact on the file server is the results CSV; there is no E119 case setup, run log, grid/convergence study, property audit or boundary-condition audit.” §10 nevertheless marks item 6 “CLOSED by this memo” and item 7 “READY TO CLOSE.” The CSV has no run ID or timestamp, as the memo's Appendix A admits.

It should state that the E119 run basis is undocumented, keep item 7 open for the E119 deliverable, and either obtain the E119 case record or label the result “not verified — run documentation missing.” The wildfire mesh log proves the wildfire case was revC; it does not prove the E119 companion run was.

**Evidence.** `E119_companion_sim_results.csv` (comments/header only; no run ID/timestamp); `Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` lines 33–35 (“Source geometry: OAS-WUI-01_revC”, “Meshing performed on: 2025-10-09 (morning)”) — this is the wildfire case; `Case/verification/three_grid_study_outputs.txt` line 2 — wildfire three-grid study; memo §5.3/Appendix A admission. `grep -ril 'E119'` finds no E119 setup or log.

### 3. MAJOR — The memo's statement that the live `Case/system/controlDict` is empty is factually wrong; the file exists and is a non-compliant fireFoam controlDict.

**What it should be.** The run geometry is 1.83 m × 2.745 m × 0.305 m (plan area 5.02 m²), only 54 % of the 3.05 m × 3.05 m (9.30 m²) tested specimen. # Independent review — CFDME-2025-041 E119 Validation Memo rev A

**Reviewed:** `/app/files/output/CFDME-2025-041_E119_Validation_Memo_revA.docx` (70 paragraphs, 11 tables, 4,759 words).  
**Review basis:** task instruction; CFDME-QA-VAL-002 rev 2 (Validation Procedure); Red Butte RBFMT-25-0918 (09/24/2025); Ironwood IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 (09/29/2025); SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01; Modeling Standard rev 4; QA Verification Standard rev 3; Units SOP rev 2; peer-review checklist; the run CSV, case files and geometry files. As-of date 10/10/2025. I did not modify any project or deliverable file.

**Overall:** The core arithmetic in the memo is correct: on the CSV as submitted, S = 130.94 min → 131 min; D = 118 min from Red Butte; E = +12.94 min → +13 min; the 10 % criterion is 11.8 min; u_val = √(4²+6²+5²) = 8.77 → ±9 min; |E| exceeds both. The memo is right that the run does **not** validate and that Bianca Rennert's 129 min is inadmissible as D under Validation Procedure §6. The findings below concern the identity/eligibility of the run, unsupported record statements, and overstatements in the memo that change the disposition and checklist conclusions.

## Findings (most serious first)

### 1. BLOCKING — The run is not the certified/tested assembly in plan size; the memo's "yes" on assembly identity is not supported and its own Table 1 contradicts it.

**Requirement.** Ironwood IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.1 states that the certification is based on a test “on a 3.05 m × 3.05 m non-load-bearing specimen of the assembly”; §1.2 states “Any deviation from the tabulated geometry places the assembly outside the scope of this certification.” Red Butte RBFMT-25-0918 §2 describes “One 3.05 m × 3.05 m (10 ft × 10 ft) specimen.” The task asks to “Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on.”

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §1: “The assembly in the run is the assembly the certification covers, within the certification’s tabulated scope.” §3 and Table 1 acknowledge that the Red Butte specimen was 3.05 m × 3.05 m while revC is a “1830 mm × 2745 mm × 305 mm panel.” §3 then says: “The certification table does not make plan size a scope parameter … If the certification is later read as requiring the 3.05 m plan size, that is a question for Ironwood, not a basis for this validation.”

**What it should be.** The run geometry is 1.83 m × 2.745 m × 0.305 m (plan area 5.02 m²), only 54 % of the 3.05 m × 3.05 m (9.30 m²) tested specimen. That is a material geometry deviation, not a through-wall detail. The memo should either (a) obtain written confirmation from Ironwood that plan size is not a certification scope parameter, or (b) state plainly that the run is outside the as-tested/certified specimen geometry, so the S/D comparison cannot be presented as a validation of the certified assembly. The top-line answer “yes” must not be given while the plan-size question is left to Ironwood; the task asked the memo to settle it.

**Evidence.** `Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Geometry/OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd`, `Document.xml`: `Width_mm = 1830`, `Height_mm = 2745`, `Thickness_mm = 305`, Description “Outer dims per WUI test panel: 1830 x 305 x 2745 mm.” Ironwood p.1 §1.1–§1.2; Red Butte p.1 §2. Plan area: 1.83 × 2.745 = 5.02 m² versus 3.05 × 3.05 = 9.30 m² (54 %).

### 2. BLOCKING — There is no documented E119 case setup, mesh, run log, or property/boundary-condition record; the memo's S is therefore not the documented S required by Validation Procedure §3, and the memo's “documented model-error finding” overstates the basis.

**Requirement.** Validation Procedure rev 2 §3: “S is the simulation prediction — the value produced by the CFD run using the model, mesh, solver, boundary conditions, and material properties documented in the report.” Every deliverable must present S, D, E, u_val “with a citation to the physical test report from which D is taken and to the run identifier from which S is taken.” Peer-review checklist item 7 requires confirmation of which OAS-WUI-01 revision matches the mesh-build timestamp in the case log. The technical-verification-review method requires “Not verified — item remains open” where the basis is missing; a missing case record cannot be closed as a documented finding.

**What the deliverable has.** §3 relies on “All case logs, the three-grid study and the deliverable manifest” to establish revC, but these are the wildfire LES artifacts. §5.3 itself states: “The only E119 companion artifact on the file server is the results CSV; there is no E119 case setup, run log, grid/convergence study, property audit or boundary-condition audit.” §10 nevertheless marks item 6 “CLOSED by this memo” and item 7 “READY TO CLOSE.” The CSV has no run ID or timestamp, as the memo's Appendix A admits.

**What it should be.** The only E119 run artifact is `E119_companion_sim_results.csv`; there is no E119 mesh/log/setup. The memo can report that the CSV's numbers fail the criterion, but it cannot call the result a “documented model-error finding” or close item 7 as an E119 geometry cross-check. It should state that the E119 run basis is undocumented, keep item 7 open for the E119 deliverable, and either obtain the E119 case record or label the result “not verified — run documentation missing.” The wildfire mesh log proves the wildfire case was revC; it does not prove the E119 companion run was.

**Evidence.** `E119_companion_sim_results.csv` (comments/header only; no run ID/timestamp); `Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` lines 33–36 (“Source geometry: OAS-WUI-01_revC”, “Meshing performed on: 2025-10-09 (morning)”) — this is the wildfire case; `Case/verification/three_grid_study_outputs.txt` line 2 — wildfire three-grid study; memo §5.3/Appendix A admission. `grep -ril 'E119'` finds no E119 setup or log.

### 3. MAJOR — The memo's statement that the live `Case/system/controlDict` is empty is factually wrong; the file exists and is a non-compliant fireFoam controlDict.

**Requirement.** Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 makes `adjustTimeStep yes`, `maxCo 0.9`, `maxDeltaT` (typically 0.01 s), `writeControl adjustableRunTime`, and a write interval capturing ≥25 samples per puffing period mandatory for transient LES; the memo §8 itself claims to check the Phase 1 setup record.

**What the deliverable has.** §8: “The live Case/system/controlDict on file is empty, and no production wildfire case setup is present.”

**What it should be.** The file is 1,310 bytes and contains `application fireFoam; endTime 2000; deltaT 0.01; adjustTimeStep no; writeControl timeStep; writeInterval 100;` with no `maxCo` or `maxDeltaT`. It is present and non-compliant, not empty. The memo should say the live controlDict exists and fails §4, and that no complete production case setup is present. This affects the Phase 1 readiness conclusion and open items 3/5.

**Evidence.** `/app/files/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system/controlDict` (1,310 bytes); firm reference `Firm/Standards/Reference_Cases/fireFoam_transient_controlDict.txt` (`adjustTimeStep yes`, `maxCo 0.9`, `maxDeltaT 0.01`, `writeControl adjustableRunTime`); Modeling Standard rev 4 §4. The document index's “0 chars” for this file is an extraction artifact, not the original.

### 4. MAJOR — The §6 argument that a revised 129 min would give a 34-min separation, while the run gives 45 min, is not evidence that 129 min is “not the record”; it is a model-shape diagnostic, not an admissibility test.

**Requirement.** Validation Procedure §6 governs substitution of D: a reissued laboratory report, a calibration certificate, and an explicit supersession statement. The acceptance tests in §5 are |E| ≤ 10 % of D and |E| against u_val; the separation between the average and single-point criteria is not an acceptance criterion.

**What the deliverable has.** §6: “If the average remains 163 min and the single-point value becomes 129 min, the test separation becomes 34 min. The run gives 45 min. The run reproduces the certified 45-min separation, not the proposed 34-min separation. That is further evidence that 129 min is not the record to validate against.”

**What it should be.** The run's 45.16-min separation is a property of the model; a properly reissued test with a 34-min separation would still be the test record. The 34 vs 45 difference would be a diagnostic of model shape, not proof that 129 min is inadmissible. The disposition on 129 min should rest solely on the §6 documentation failure (which it does); the “further evidence” sentence should be deleted or reframed. As written, it is an unsupported conclusion.

**Evidence.** Validation Procedure §6; memo Table 6 (original 163−118 = 45 min; revised 163−129 = 34 min); run CSV 176.10−130.94 = 45.16 min. The run's separation is independent of which D is adopted.

### 5. MAJOR — u_val uses firm defaults, but the required project-specific tabulation in the project QA folder is not recorded; the memo admits no project-specific E119 study is on file.

**Requirement.** Validation Procedure §4: “A project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, u_exp shall be recorded in the project QA folder before u_val is published.” The same section permits firm defaults but still requires the project-specific tabulation and independence verification at peer review.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent checks for the CFDME-2025-041 E119 validation memo.
Recomputes the governing crossings from the run CSV, reads the submitted DOCX back,
and tests the memo's declared values against the Validation Procedure limits and
the record values. Prints the worst case per limit with utilisation."""
import csv, math, re, sys
from docx import Document

RUN='/app/files/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Validation/E119_companion_sim_results.csv'
MEMO='/app/files/output/CFDME-2025-041_E119_Validation_Memo_revA.docx'

# --- read run ---
rows=[]
for line in open(RUN):
    if line.startswith('#') or not line.strip(): continue
    rows.append(line.strip().split(','))
hdr=rows[0]; data=[dict(zip(hdr,map(float,r))) for r in rows[1:]]
def cross(col,thr):
    for a,b in zip(data,data[1:]):
        if a[col] < thr <= b[col]:
            return a['time_min']+(thr-a[col])/(b[col]-a[col])
    raise ValueError('no crossing')
def interp(col,t):
    for a,b in zip(data,data[1:]):
        if a['time_min'] <= t <= b['time_min']:
            return a[col]+(b[col]-a[col])*(t-a['time_min'])/(b['time_min']-a['time_min'])
    raise ValueError('out of range')
S=cross('T_unexposed_max_C',202.0)
Savg=cross('T_unexposed_avg_C',160.0)
mean_at_S=interp('T_unexposed_avg_C',S)-21.0
D=118.0; Davg=163.0
E=S-D; crit=0.10*D; u=math.sqrt(4**2+6**2+5**2)
largest_primary=D+crit
largest_u=D+9.0
sep_test=Davg-D; sep_run=Savg-S
hot_test=181.0-96.0; hot_run=181.0-mean_at_S

# --- read memo ---
doc=Document(MEMO)
text='\n'.join([p.text for p in doc.paragraphs])
for t in doc.tables:
    for r in t.rows:
        text+='\n'+' | '.join(c.text for c in r.cells)

checks=[]
def check(name, condition, detail):
    checks.append((name,bool(condition),detail))

# schema/content presence
for required in [
    'does not validate', 'S = 131 min (130.94 min by interpolation)', 'D = 118 min', 'E = S − D = +13 min (+12.94 min unrounded)',
    '11.8 min', '±9 min', '129.8 min', '127 min', '45 min', '85 °C', '91 °C',
    '1-hour (60 min)', '2-hour', 'RBFMT-25-0918', 'IWFPE-CERT-25-0374',
    'CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others.',
    'OAS-WUI-01_revC', 'OAS-WUI-01_revD', '610 mm', '3355 mm', '1830 mm', '2745 mm',
    'Bianca', 'Item 6', 'Item 7', 'Items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9', 'no E119 rework has started',
    'wildfire', 'E = S − D', 'u_val',
]:
    check('memo contains '+required, required.lower() in text.lower(), 'required phrase missing' if required.lower() not in text.lower() else 'present')

# recompute comparisons and check memo wording
check('S whole-minute = 131', round(S)==131, f'S={S:.5f}')
check('Savg whole-minute = 176', round(Savg)==176, f'Savg={Savg:.5f}')
check('E reported = +13', round(E)==13, f'E={E:.5f}')
check('E unrounded > criterion', abs(E)>crit, f'|E|={abs(E):.5f} vs {crit:.3f}')
check('E > u_val', abs(E)>u, f'|E|={abs(E):.5f} vs {u:.5f}')
check('largest primary = 129.8', abs(largest_primary-129.8)<1e-9, f'{largest_primary:.3f}')
check('largest within u = 127', abs(largest_u-127.0)<1e-9, f'{largest_u:.3f}')
check('test separation = 45', abs(sep_test-45.0)<1e-9, f'{sep_test:.3f}')
check('run separation rounds 45', round(sep_run)==45, f'{sep_run:.5f}')
check('hot test = 85', abs(hot_test-85.0)<1e-9, f'{hot_test:.3f}')
check('hot run rounds 91', round(hot_run)==91, f'{hot_run:.5f}')

# parse key rollup table (Table 4) and compare
# table order: headers then rows
rollup={}
for t in doc.tables:
    if t.rows and t.rows[0].cells[0].text.strip()=='Quantity':
        for r in t.rows[1:]:
            rollup[r.cells[0].text.strip()]=r.cells[1].text.strip()
check('rollup table S value', rollup.get('S — simulation prediction (single-point)','').startswith('131'), rollup.get('S — simulation prediction (single-point)',''))
check('rollup table D value', rollup.get('D — certified experimental value','')=='118', rollup.get('D — certified experimental value',''))
check('rollup table E value', rollup.get('E = S − D','').startswith('+13'), rollup.get('E = S − D',''))
check('rollup u value', '±9' in rollup.get('u_val — combined validation uncertainty',''), rollup.get('u_val — combined validation uncertainty',''))
check('rollup criterion', '11.8' in rollup.get('Primary acceptance criterion',''), rollup.get('Primary acceptance criterion',''))
check('rollup largest primary', '129.8' in rollup.get('Largest S clearing the primary criterion',''), rollup.get('Largest S clearing the primary criterion',''))
check('rollup largest u', rollup.get('Largest S that is also within u_val','').startswith('127'), rollup.get('Largest S that is also within u_val',''))

# hard-limit utilisation table (worst case per limit)
limits=[
    ('|E| <= 10% D (primary)', abs(E), crit),
    ('|E| <= u_val (secondary)', abs(E), u),
    ('S <= largest S for primary', S, largest_primary),
    ('S <= largest S within u_val', S, largest_u),
]
print('Hard-limit checks (utilisation = demand/limit):')
for name,demand,limit in limits:
    util=demand/limit
    status='PASS' if demand<=limit+1e-12 else 'FAIL'
    print(f'  {name}: demand={demand:.3f} min, limit={limit:.3f} min, utilisation={util:.4f}, {status}')

# comparison checks
print('Comparison checks:')
for name,val,criterion in [
    ('test vs run separation difference (min)',abs(sep_run-sep_test),0.5),
    ('hot-spot margin difference (°C)',abs(hot_run-hot_test),10.0),
]:
    util=val/criterion
    print(f'  {name}: difference={val:.3f}, allowance={criterion:.1f}, utilisation={util:.4f}, {"PASS" if val<=criterion else "FAIL"}')

# show failures
fails=[c for c in checks if not c[1]]
print(f'\nContent checks: {len(checks)-len(fails)}/{len(checks)} passed')
for name,ok,detail in fails:
    print('  FAIL:',name,'|',detail)
if fails:
    sys.exit(1)
print('ALL MEMO CONTENT CHECKS PASSED')

# ---- additional hard-case checks (all D scenarios in the record) ----
print('\nScenario table for D:')
scenarios=[('Certified D=118',118.0),('Bianca D=129 (inadmissible)',129.0)]
worst=None
for label,Dx in scenarios:
    Ex=S-Dx; cx=0.10*Dx
    util_primary=abs(Ex)/cx; util_u=abs(Ex)/u
    status='PASS' if (abs(Ex)<=cx and abs(Ex)<=u) else 'FAIL'
    print(f'  {label}: S={S:.3f} min, E={Ex:+.3f} min, criterion={cx:.3f} min, u_val={u:.3f} min, util_primary={util_primary:.4f}, util_u={util_u:.4f}, {status}')
    score=max(util_primary,util_u)
    if worst is None or score>worst[0]: worst=(score,label,Ex,cx)
print(f'  Worst case: {worst[1]} with E={worst[2]:+.3f} min, criterion={worst[3]:.3f} min, utilisation={worst[0]:.4f}')

# ---- assembly parameter check from revC/revD FCStd ----
import zipfile, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
def fcstd_props(path):
    z=zipfile.ZipFile(path); root=ET.fromstring(z.read('Document.xml'))
    out={}
    for el in root.iter():
        name=el.get('name')
        if name and el.tag.endswith('Property'):
            for child in el:
                if child.tag.endswith('Float') and child.get('value') is not None:
                    out[name]=float(child.get('value'))
    return out
base='/app/files/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Geometry/'
revC=fcstd_props(base+'OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd')
revD=fcstd_props(base+'OAS-WUI-01_revD.FCStd')
print('\nAssembly geometry checks:')
for key,expected in [('Wythe_mm',50.0),('AirGap_mm',205.0),('Thickness_mm',305.0),('TieSpacingVertical_mm',600.0),('TieEmbedment_mm',25.0),('Width_mm',1830.0),('Height_mm',2745.0)]:
    val=revC.get(key)
    print(f'  revC {key}: {val} mm (expected {expected} mm) {"PASS" if val==expected else "FAIL"}')
for key,expected in [('ParapetHeight_mm',610.0),('TotalHeight_mm',3355.0),('Coping_mm',50.0),('CopingOverhang_mm',25.0),('Thickness_mm',305.0)]:

1. Basis of Certification
This certification is issued on the basis of one certified third-party fire-endurance test performed on the wall assembly
identified below.
1.1 Certified test of record. Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing, Report No. RBFMT-25-0918, test date 09/24/2025,
report issued 09/24/2025 ("the Red Butte test report"). The report documents one vertical fire-endurance test
performed in accordance with ASTM E119, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests of Building Construction and
Materials, on a 3.05 m × 3.05 m non-load-bearing specimen of the assembly.
1.2 Assembly description. The assembly is a double-wythe 3D-printed concrete wall consisting of two printed
concrete leaves separated by an open-air cavity and connected by continuous truss-type galvanized steel wall ties.
The as-tested geometry, taken from Section 2 of the Red Butte test report and reproduced here as the certified
geometry, is:

Parameter                                                    Value
Leaf thickness (each of two leaves)                          50 mm
Cavity width (open air, no fill, no membrane)                205 mm
Overall specimen thickness                                   305 mm (50 / 205 / 50)
Aggregate                                                    Siliceous
Tie material                                                 Galvanized steel, truss-type (triangular zigzag),
                                                             continuous
Tie wire gauge / diameter                                    9-gauge (3.8 mm)
Tie vertical spacing                                         600 mm o.c.
Tie embedment into each leaf                                 25 mm
Cavity contents                                              Open air; no insulation, no fill, no fire-stop

Any deviation from the tabulated geometry places the assembly outside the scope of this certification.
1.3 Test conditions of record. Non-load-bearing configuration, standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve
applied to the exposed face, no applied mechanical load, no hose-stream retest contracted. Furnace deviation was
within the ASTM E119 tolerance band for the full duration of the test.

2. Governing Endurance Result
ASTM E119 was applied to the specimen described in Section 1.2 above. Two thermal-transmission criteria apply to
a non-load-bearing wall under ASTM E119, and the earlier of the two governs the reported fire endurance:
• Average unexposed-face criterion — the nine-thermocouple mean rise shall not exceed 139 °C above initial
   ambient. Per Section 5.1 of the Red Butte test report, the average criterion was reached at 163 min after test
   start.
• Single-point criterion — the rise at any single thermocouple on the unexposed face shall not exceed 181 °C
   above initial ambient. Per Section 5.2 of the Red Butte test report, the single-point criterion was reached at 118
   min after test start at thermocouple 6, which was positioned directly opposite a horizontal course of the 3.8 mm
   truss-type steel wall ties described in Section 1.2 above.


--- page 2 ---
Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two criteria governs the reported fire endurance. The single-point criterion was
reached first, and therefore the measured fire endurance of the assembly is 118 min.
The single-point governance at thermocouple 6 is consistent with the presence of the continuous steel tie course as a
metallic thermal-bridge path between the exposed and unexposed leaves at that location. The average
unexposed-face temperature rise across the remaining eight thermocouples did not approach the single-point
criterion at the moment of governance and is a distinct and later-occurring result, as documented in Section 5 of the
Red Butte test report.

3. Certification
On the basis of the certified test identified in Section 1.1 and the governing endurance result stated in Section 2,
Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering certifies the assembly for a 1-hour fire-resistance rating (60 min).
The measured endurance of 118 min exceeds the 60-minute rung by a healthy margin. The next higher standard rung
is a 2-hour rating, which requires 120 min of demonstrated endurance under the governing criterion; the measured
endurance falls short of that rung by 2 min. Because the certified rating is limited by the governing single-point result
to the highest standard rung fully demonstrated by the certified test, the assembly is certified at 1-hour and not at any
higher rung.
Certification scope. This certification is limited to the specific assembly and test conditions described in Sections 1.2
and 1.3. It is not a statement about any other assembly, any other configuration of ties, cavity contents, leaf
thickness, or aggregate, or any other fire exposure than the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve.

4. Amendments and Reissuance
Any change to the certified rating requires a reissued test report from the testing laboratory of record and a new
certification issued by Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering. No other party may certify or restate this rating.

5. Limitations
5.1 Standard exposure only. The certified rating is a comparative assembly rating derived from performance under
the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve as delivered by a laboratory furnace. It is a measure of the
thermal-transmission behavior of the specific assembly described in Section 1.2 under a standard fire exposure.
5.2 Not a wildfire-performance statement. The ASTM E119 exposure is a standardized post-flashover
compartment-fire curve. It is not representative of a wildland-urban-interface (WUI) wildfire exposure, which involves
radiant and convective heat loading from an advancing vegetation fire, a distinct heat-flux history, wind-driven flame
tilt, and firebrand deposition, among other phenomena not present in the E119 furnace test. Nothing in this
certification should be read as a WUI wildfire survival prediction for the assembly, the structures in which the
assembly is installed, or the occupants of those structures.
5.3 Non-load-bearing configuration. The assembly was tested and is certified in a non-load-bearing configuration
only. Loaded configurations require a separate load-bearing test and a separate certification.
5.4 No hose-stream criterion. No hose-stream retest was contracted or performed. Where a jurisdiction or code
requires a hose-stream criterion in addition to thermal transmission, that requirement is not addressed by this
certification.
5.5 As-built conformance. This certification presupposes that the assembly installed in the field conforms to the
geometry and materials described in Section 1.2. Field verification of conformance is the responsibility of the design
and construction team of record for each installation.

Conducted For: Ocotillo Additive Structures 3175 S Palo Verde Rd Tucson, AZ 85713
Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing Salt Lake City, UT


TABLE OF CONTENTS
1. Test Standard and Method 2. Specimen Description 3. Instrumentation 4. Test Conduct 5. Results 6. Conclusion 7.
Instrumentation Calibration Certificates Signatures


1. TEST STANDARD AND METHOD
The evaluation reported here was performed in accordance with ASTM E119, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests
of Building Construction and Materials (current edition). One vertical fire-endurance test was performed on the wall
assembly described in Section 2, using the standard time-temperature curve prescribed by ASTM E119. The
exposed face of the assembly was subjected to the E119 standard curve delivered by the laboratory's natural-gas
vertical wall furnace, with furnace temperatures monitored by nine furnace thermocouples symmetrically distributed
on the exposed face per the standard.
The assembly was tested as a non-load-bearing partition. The applicable fire-endurance criteria for a
non-load-bearing wall under ASTM E119 are the following two thermal-transmission conditions on the unexposed
face:
• Average unexposed-face criterion. The average temperature rise measured by nine thermocouples
   symmetrically disposed on the unexposed face of the specimen shall not exceed 139 degC (250 degF) above the
   initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.
• Single-point criterion. The temperature rise at any single thermocouple on the unexposed face shall not exceed
   181 degC (325 degF) above the initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.
Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two thermal-transmission criteria governs the reported fire endurance for the
specimen.


2. SPECIMEN DESCRIPTION
One 3.05 m × 3.05 m (10 ft × 10 ft) specimen was constructed by the client at the Red Butte laboratory prior to test.
The specimen is a double-wythe 3D-printed concrete wall assembly consisting of two printed concrete leaves
separated by an open-air cavity and connected by continuous truss-type steel ties.

2.1 Concrete leaves
• Number of leaves: two, oriented parallel and in registration.
• Leaf thickness: each leaf 50 mm as printed and cured (siliceous aggregate mix).
• Aggregate: siliceous.
• Placement: wet-on-wet extruded 3D printing; nominal 20 mm bead pitch; leaves printed vertically on the
   specimen frame and cured to the manufacturer's 28-day protocol prior to shipment for test.

2.2 Cavity


--- page 2 ---
• Cavity width: 205 mm between the interior surfaces of the two leaves.
• Cavity contents: open air. No insulation, no fill, no membrane, no fire-stop material was present in the cavity as
   constructed for this test.

2.3 Overall specimen thickness
• Overall: 305 mm (50 + 205 + 50).
2.4 Wall ties
Continuous truss-type (triangular zigzag) ties fabricated from 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized steel wire connect the
two leaves. Tie schedule:
Parameter                                                   Value
Material                                                    Galvanized steel, truss-type (triangular zigzag),
                                                            continuous
Wire gauge                                                  9-gauge
Wire diameter                                               3.8 mm
Vertical spacing                                            600 mm o.c.
Horizontal extent                                           Continuous, full specimen width
Embedment into each leaf                                    25 mm

Ties were placed by the client at each 600 mm horizontal course during printing of the leaves and were embedded 25
mm into the printed concrete on each side.


3. INSTRUMENTATION
Instrumentation on the unexposed face was applied by Red Butte technicians per ASTM E119. All thermocouples
were Type K, 20 AWG, glass-braid insulated, fixed to the unexposed face of the specimen with pads per the
standard.

3.1 Unexposed-face thermocouple layout
Nine thermocouples, designated TC-1 through TC-9, were installed on the unexposed face in the symmetric pattern
prescribed by ASTM E119: one thermocouple at the geometric center of the specimen, four at the midpoints of
imaginary quadrants, and four additional thermocouples such that no thermocouple lies within 305 mm (12 in) of a
specimen edge and thermocouples are approximately equidistant from one another. The average of the readings
from TC-1 through TC-9 is the value used for the average unexposed-face criterion.
A tenth thermocouple, TC-10, was installed as a single-point plotter and continuous strip-chart reference; TC-10
readings are recorded but are not part of the nine-thermocouple average.

3.2 Position of TC-6 relative to tie course
The specimen was surveyed for tie positions before instrumentation was applied. During layout of the nine
unexposed-face thermocouples, thermocouple 6 fell over one of the horizontal courses of steel wall ties: TC-6 is
located directly opposite a 3.8 mm truss-type tie embedded in the outer (unexposed) leaf. This positioning is retained
as the E119 symmetric layout was applied without adjustment; the location is documented in the plan diagram below.

3.3 Plan diagram callout (unexposed face)


--- page 3 ---
UNEXPOSED FACE - PLAN LAYOUT (viewed from unexposed side)

                                          TC-1                     TC-2                      TC-3




                                          TC-4                     TC-5        TC-10         TC-6
                                                                                                                  tie course
                                                                                                                  600 mm o.c.
                                                                                                                  (9-gauge, 3.8 mm)
                                          TC-7                     TC-8                      TC-9




                                      TC-10 (plotter reference, near geometric center) not part of the nine-thermocouple average.


Legend: circle = thermocouple on plain concrete; square = TC-6, positioned over a horizontal truss-type tie course.


The tie course crossing behind TC-6 constitutes a metallic path from the exposed leaf to the unexposed leaf at that
location. Readings from TC-6 are therefore expected to reflect the local thermal signature of that path and are
reported alongside the eight other unexposed-face thermocouples without adjustment or omission.

3.4 Furnace and ambient instrumentation
• Nine furnace thermocouples (TCF-1 through TCF-9) per E119, symmetrically placed within 6 in of the exposed
   face, monitored delivery of the standard time-temperature curve.
• Two ambient thermocouples (TC-A1, TC-A2) recorded laboratory ambient at the unexposed side, from which the
   initial ambient reference used for the rise criteria was derived.
• Initial ambient (average of TC-A1, TC-A2 at t = 0): 21.0 degC.
3.5 Data acquisition
All thermocouple channels were logged at 1 Hz to a computerized data acquisition system with NIST-traceable
channel calibration. TC-10 was additionally recorded on an independent single-point strip-chart plotter to provide a
mechanical secondary trace.


4. TEST CONDUCT
The instrumented specimen was mounted in the laboratory's vertical wall furnace on the morning of 09/24/2025. The
exposed face was oriented toward the furnace chamber. The specimen was clamped at the perimeter with the same
frame and gasket detail routinely used for non-load-bearing partition specimens at this laboratory.
The furnace was ignited and the exposed face was subjected to the ASTM E119 standard time-temperature curve
from t = 0 onward. Furnace temperatures tracked the standard curve within the tolerance band prescribed by ASTM
E119 for the full duration of the test (deviation area within the specified 10% at 1 hr and 7.5% at 2 hr and beyond).
The specimen was monitored continuously. The test was conducted to termination on the governing
thermal-transmission criterion as defined in Section 1 above; no hose-stream retest was performed as none was
contracted. No load was applied to the specimen (non-load-bearing configuration).
Test start: 09:02 MDT, 09/24/2025. Test termination: 11:00 MDT, 09/24/2025 (118 min after start), at which point the
governing thermal-transmission criterion was reached. Data acquisition continued for 45 additional minutes past
termination to characterize the full unexposed-face response, at which point the average-rise criterion was also
reached (see Section 5).


5. RESULTS
5.1 Average unexposed-face temperature rise (nine-thermocouple mean)
The arithmetic mean of TC-1 through TC-9, expressed as rise above the initial ambient of 21.0 degC, is the value
evaluated against the average criterion.


--- page 4 ---
• Criterion: 139 degC (250 degF) rise above initial ambient.
• The nine-thermocouple mean rise reached 139 degC at 163 min after test start.
5.2 Single-point unexposed-face temperature rise
The maximum rise across the nine unexposed-face thermocouples, at each instant, was tracked continuously against
the single-point criterion.
• Criterion: 181 degC (325 degF) rise above initial ambient.
• The maximum rise reached 181 degC at 118 min after test start.
• Governing thermocouple at the moment the criterion was reached: thermocouple 6, positioned over a horizontal
   steel tie course as described in Section 3.2 and shown in the plan diagram.
At 118 min, TC-6 recorded 181 degC rise above ambient while the nine-thermocouple mean rise stood at
approximately 96 degC. The remaining eight unexposed-face thermocouples (TC-1 through TC-5 and TC-7 through
TC-9) had not individually reached the single-point limit at that time. TC-10 (single-point plotter, near geometric
center) tracked closely with the mean of TC-1 through TC-9 throughout.

5.3 Governing endurance
Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two thermal-transmission criteria governs the reported fire endurance:

 Criterion                                Value                                    Time reached
 Average unexposed-face rise              139 degC                                 163 min
 (nine-TC mean)
 Single-point rise (any single TC)        181 degC                                 118 min (at thermocouple 6)

The single-point criterion was reached first at 118 min and therefore governs the reported fire endurance for this
specimen.
> Reported endurance D = 118 min.


6. CONCLUSION
Under the conditions of ASTM E119 (standard time-temperature curve, non-load-bearing, no applied load, no
hose-stream retest contracted), the double-wythe 3D-printed concrete wall assembly described in Section 2 exhibited
a measured fire endurance of 118 min, governed by the single-point criterion at thermocouple 6, which was
positioned over a horizontal truss-type steel tie course. The average unexposed-face criterion was reached later at
163 min and does not govern.
This report documents the measured thermal-transmission behavior of the specimen tested. Certification of a
fire-resistance rating for the assembly is the domain of the certifying fire-protection engineer of record for the project
and is not within the scope of this laboratory or this report.


7. INSTRUMENTATION CALIBRATION CERTIFICATES
All thermocouples and data-acquisition channels employed on this test were calibrated per Red Butte's
NIST-traceable procedure within the 90 days preceding the test date. Certificates on file at the laboratory and
